axes.label: Model
axes.description: Promises on the objective, payoff, or operator. Convex feasible sets and convex lower-level objectives are not automatically convex target objectives.

groups.label: Objective convexity
groups.description: Convexity of the same objective being minimized (or per-round loss). Strong convexity implies convexity on that same domain. This excludes only-convex feasible sets and only-convex lower-level g in a bilevel problem.

options.label: Convex objective
options.description: Same-target convexity, including certified same-target strong convexity; not merely convex geometry or a convex lower problem.

options.label: Strongly convex objective
options.description: Strong convexity of the target objective on its declared domain.

options.label: Weakly convex objective
options.description: Explicit weak-convexity promise on the target objective.

options.label: Convexity not assumed
options.description: Convexity is explicitly not promised; this does not assert that every individual function is nonconvex.

groups.label: Problem structure
groups.description: Declared payoff, finite-sum or composite structure, without asserting a different objective or oracle.

options.label: Convex–concave payoff
options.description: Explicit source-declared structure: Convex–concave payoff.

options.label: Composite objective
options.description: Explicit source-declared structure: Composite objective.

groups.label: Operator monotonicity
groups.description: Monotonicity of the declared target operator. Strong monotonicity implies monotonicity for that same operator.

options.label: Monotone operator
options.description: Applies to the declared target operator; no scalar-potential assumption is inferred.

options.label: Strongly monotone operator
options.description: Applies to the declared target operator; no scalar-potential assumption is inferred.

axes.label: Oracle
axes.description: Declared primitive oracle interface. Public geometric auxiliaries do not determine the quality of the unknown-object feedback.

groups.label: Oracle access
groups.description: For scalar primitives, the highest declared derivative-access family: zeroth order includes derivative-free value, component-value and comparison replies, not only full values. Operator/matrix and online protocols are named separately when no scalar order is normalized. Vector-operator order zero is not scalar-objective zeroth order. Exact parameterized orders remain in advanced detail.

groups.label: Primitive feedback quality

filter_semantics.aliases: Exact natural phrases with longest-phrase matching; never substring-match convex inside nonconvex, exact inside inexact, or access order inside first-order stationarity.
